summary: The article provides a largely accurate and well-explained overview of the CBDT's new crypto reporting guidance, aligning with OECD standards, and its implications for Indian investors.

claims.claim: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued guidance aligning India's crypto reporting with global OECD standards.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm CBDT has issued guidance aligning with OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF).

claims.claim: It does not introduce new taxes on crypto assets; existing tax laws remain unchanged.
claims.note: The guidance is procedural and does not change existing crypto taxation (30% tax on gains, 1% TDS).

claims.claim: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has operationalised a comprehensive guidance note for the reporting of crypto-asset transactions in India. This framework is a direct adoption of the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF)
claims.note: The CBDT has indeed released a guidance note operationalizing India's crypto-asset reporting framework in line with OECD CARF.

claims.claim: While the guidance itself doesn't alter the existing tax provisions for Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs) – which include a 30% tax on gains and 1% TDS on certain transactions
claims.note: Income from VDA transfer is taxed at 30% (plus surcharge and cess) and 1% TDS is applicable on VDA transactions under Section 115BBH and 194S respectively.

claims.claim: Under current VDA tax rules, losses from one VDA cannot be set off against gains from another VDA, nor against any other income.
claims.note: Section 115BBH explicitly states that losses from the transfer of VDAs cannot be set off against any other income, including gains from other VDAs, and cannot be carried forward.

claims.claim: Under Section 509 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, exchanges will file this information annually through Form 167, starting with transactions from calendar year 2026 and the first filings due in 2027
claims.note: Sources confirm that reporting obligations are under Section 509 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and Rules 241 to 244 and Form 167 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026, with reporting starting from calendar year 2026 and first filings due in 2027.

article_title: CBDT's New Crypto Reporting Guidance: What Investors Need to Know
